QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_5

question.text: Swasth Bharat Trust's SIA sample was 5% of direct beneficiaries in the AB Responsible Services IWMP case. For an assessment under SAS-100 of a 25,000-person programme, what is a defensible MINIMUM sample size the SIA should target, assuming 95% confidence, 5% margin of error and a conservatively assumed 50% proportion?

answer.text: Approximately 378 respondents (rounded up from Cochran formula at finite-population correction)

explanation.text: The Logic: For a statistically defensible sample size you must define a confidence level (e.g., 95%), a margin of error (e.g., 5%) and an assumed population proportion (p = 0.5 for the most conservative result). Using the standard Cochran sample-size formula n0 = z² · p · (1-p) / e² gives 1.96² · 0.5 · 0.5 / 0.05² ≈ 384, and applying a finite-population correction for N = 25,000 yields approximately 378 respondents. This is the statistically defensible minimum, independent of the 5%-rule-of-thumb actually used in the case. The Trap: Option D (a flat 5% = 1,250) is what the case text recites as the SE's internal sampling, but is a rule of thumb rather than a statistical minimum. Options B and C fall well short of the required precision at 95% confidence and 5% margin of error. Note: The cited SIA workbook supports the requirement to define confidence interval and margin of error for statistically significant sampling and mentions the IWMP 5%/500-survey approach, but does not present the Cochran finite-population formula or the 378-respondent result. The calculation above is drawn from general statistical practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
